function_extent.listing_reexported: GhidraMCP /read_memory over 7 bytes at 0x0104c110 returned 8b 81 10 02 00 00 c3, and /disassemble_function returned exactly two instructions at 0x0104c110 and 0x0104c116. The two agree byte for byte. Decoding the MOV by hand: 8B is MOV r32,r/m32; 81 gives mod = 10 (32-bit displacement follows), reg = 000 (EAX) and rm = 001 (ECX); 10 02 00 00 is the little-endian disp32 = 0x210; C3 is a near return with no immediate. abi_derived.parse independently declares 2 instructions with degraded = false, unparsed = 0 and flow_complete = true, so the listing is the whole of the body and not a slice of it -- which is what licenses claiming there is no third instruction after the RET.

observed_original_abi.receiver_alias: R-DIRECT, no alias: the body never copies ECX into a scratch register
observed_original_abi.prologue: none. There is no frame: no PUSH of a saved register, no stack allocation, no SEH cookie, no fs:[0] install (abi_derived.frame is all false/null and seh_or_cookie_frame is absent).
observed_original_abi.ghidra_convention_note: Ghidra records no calling convention and no parameter count for this VA (ghidra_has_calling_convention = false, ghidra_calling_convention_signal = no_information), and its prototype's 'void' parameter list is what an unanalysed stub looks like; it is cross-validation-only and is not used as an oracle here. The convention below comes from the machine ABI record's own evidence: the receiver arrives in ECX and is dereferenced, and the terminator carries no imm16.
observed_original_abi.dispatch: none. indirect_calls 0, vtable_shaped_loads 0, call_offsets []. No CALL, JMP or indirect transfer appears in the two-instruction listing, and neither 0xE8 nor 0xFF occurs anywhere in the seven bytes.

abi.return_type_basis: THIS IS A SOURCE-SIDE CHOICE, NOT A MACHINE FINDING, AND IT IS RECORDED AS ONE. The machine fixes the WIDTH: EAX's only definition is the dword load at 0x0104c110 and obs-0002 records it as a definite mem_load, so the returned value is 4 bytes (return_width_bytes = 4, return.aggregate_evidence.bulk_write = false, sret.present = false, return.void_possible = false). The machine does NOT fix the element type: abi_derived.return.type is null, its register_class is the inference string 'pointer_like' at INFERRED confidence, and the one direct caller tests the result with a signed JLE and stores it into a 4-byte member of the same object. Those two readings are in tension and the evidence does not settle it, so the reconstruction returns an opaque 4-byte alias named FieldWord and the model test asserts the bit pattern and the width only. A reviewer should read return_type = 'FieldWord' as '4 bytes, element type unresolved', not as a claim that the 32 bits are an unsigned integer, a signed integer or a pointer.

mechanics.control_flow: none. The listing holds no conditional branch, no jump and no call, so the body is straight-line by the listing's own evidence rather than by assumption. The unconditional fall-through is the RET.
mechanics.branch_decision: there is no branch to decide, and none was invented. In particular there is no null check on the receiver: the body compares nothing before dereferencing ECX, and a reconstruction that returned 0 for a null receiver would be a structure the two-instruction listing cannot contain. The model test asserts the fault instead (mutation m6).
mechanics.constants: one, the displacement 0x210 (528), encoded in the instruction's disp32 field. There is no immediate, no constant load and no arithmetic, so the returned value is memory-dependent and this is NOT a constant stub.
mechanics.not_modelled: the meaning of the returned 32 bits; the name of the field at +0x210; the name of the class; the receiver's extent beyond 0x214; the vtable pointer at +0x00 (never read by this body).
mechanics.globals: none. The xref export carries no data-reference edge type at all (dependencies.data_reference_count = 0) and the two-instruction listing names no absolute address, so the absence of a global is claimed from the listing alone and is not corroborated by a second machine side that does not exist.
mechanics.direct_calls: none. The xref export records no outgoing edge for this VA; dependencies.edges holds only the two incoming call edges from 0x00ff3df0.
mechanics.return_semantics_machine: EAX, 4 bytes, the value loaded from the receiver at +0x210. The ABI envelope classifies the register as pointer_like at INFERRED confidence and leaves the element type null.
mechanics.receiver_writes: none. written_through = 0, and the listing's only memory operand is the load itself. This is a pure read, asserted two ways in the model test: a whole-arena byte snapshot, and a PROT_READ mapping of the receiver so that a store of the same value would still fault.

return_semantics.value: the 32 bits at receiver + 0x210, returned bit-exact in EAX with no extension, truncation, normalisation or byte swap. The value is whatever the receiver's memory holds: it depends on no constant and on no callee, which is the fact that separates this body from a constant stub and the model test sweeps ten values through it to prove it.
return_semantics.ownership: no reference acquisition, release or copy of any kind. The value is a copy of 4 bytes out of an object the body does not own and does not retain; the body stores nothing anywhere.
return_semantics.lifetime: the returned 32 bits outlive nothing and refer to nothing on the machine evidence. The only direct caller stores them into a 4-byte member of another object (0x00ff3e41), which is an observation about that caller and not a claim about this body's element type.

tools/reconstruction_tooling/validate.py, read to establish which source shape each of the checks can and cannot adjudicate BEFORE writing the source, and specifically that the constant scan, the field-declaration scan, the callee scan, the data-address scan and the virtual-slot scan all run on the target span with comments stripped -- which is why the span's own code carries exactly one hex literal (0x210), exactly one displacement, no address-suffixed callee and no slot token, while the neighbouring addresses this package discusses live in the header and in these notes
unresolved_questions: What is the ELEMENT TYPE of the returned 32 bits? The machine fixes the width (4 bytes) and nothing else: abi_derived.return.type is null and its register_class is the inference string 'pointer_like' at INFERRED confidence, while the one direct caller tests the result with a signed JLE and stores it into a 4-byte member. A signed integer, an unsigned handle and a pointer all survive every fact in the evidence set. Settling it needs either a second direct caller that uses the value as an address, or a record of what the caller at 0x00ff3df0 was doing with the object it got from the 0x00ff3e13 virtual call.

Is 0x00ff3df0 the only direct caller? The xref export records exactly one, but it is a projection and this package did not re-derive the whole image's call sites independently. A vtable slot is also reachable indirectly, so the set of call sites reaching this body through the table at 0x01490be8 is not enumerated here.

What is the class? The triage record carries sdk_name = null, the Sporepedia cluster label is a classifier output rather than a symbol, and no RTTI exists in this binary. The receiver is therefore an opaque 0x214-byte run and nothing in this package names it. The vtable at 0x01490be8 and the sibling at 0x00641770 narrow it but do not identify it.

How large is the receiver really? Only that it is at least 0x214 bytes is established. The one caller touches +0x60, +0x64 and +0x7c, all inside that, so the true extent is larger and is not modelled.

Is +0x210 a field of its own or part of a larger sub-object (a refcount, a size, a capacity, an index, a version)? A two-instruction accessor cannot see this. Other bodies in the same class would have to establish it, and none was re-read for this package.

conditions: The original process is driven to a 0x01490be8 object and this body is called through the table's slot +0x14 with the receiver's +0x210 word set to a known non-zero pattern.

A trace records the receiver address in ECX, the four bytes read at receiver+0x210, and the full 32-bit value of EAX at 0x0104c116, to confirm the load is 4 bytes and that nothing modifies it between the load and the return.
A trace records what the caller at 0x00ff3e2d branches on and what it later stores at 0x00ff3e41, which is the only evidence in the set that bears on the element type.

validation.model_test: plain int main() with explicit checks, no framework and no external dependency; returns non-zero on any failure. This body has no direct callee, so there is no callee observer to define, and the test asserts that absence positively instead (see mutation_checking). Ten decoy classes, each with a discrimination assertion proving the fixture actually separates the correct answer from the wrong one: D1 displacement (neighbour decoys at +0x00/+0x60/+0x64/+0x7c/+0x1fc/+0x208/+0x20c/+0x214/+0x218/+0x224, plus byte-granularity slips at 0x20f and 0x211); D2 width and lanes (0x11223344 for the byte lanes, 0x80000000 and 0x7fffffff for the top bit, 0xffffffff for the all-bits case, 0x0000ffff and 0xffff0000 for the halves, and a byte-swap check); D3 one level vs two levels (a POINTER planted at +0x210 pointing at a poisoned cell, so a two-level model returns the poison; plus the zero case, run in a forked child because a two-level model faults rather than returns); D4 the receiver is the object and not a pointer (a decoy object reachable through the receiver's first word, with its own +0x210 field holding a different value); D5 not a constant stub (a ten-value sweep plus two arenas differing only at +0x210, which must give different answers); D6 no write at all (whole-arena byte snapshot, plus a PROT_READ mapping of the receiver so a same-value write-back would still fault -- a gap the first mutation round found and this assertion closed); D7 the read stays inside the object (the receiver placed so it ends exactly at a PROT_NONE guard page, exercised in a child); D8 no invented null guard (a null receiver must fault with SIGSEGV, in a child, asserted rather than documented); D9 no transfer in the encoding (a byte scan of the seven original bytes for the CALL/dispatch opcodes); D10 the declared ABI surface (a one-parameter thiscall function-pointer type the reconstruction must be assignable to, and the return width).

PROMOTION GATE BLOCKER (clang++ -Wall -Wextra -Werror -m32, static-library link + CTest) REMOVED by repair worker rp15 on 2026-09-28. Cause: the model test's own copy of the receiver extent, `constexpr std::size_t kReceiverBytes = 0x214;` in the test TU's anonymous namespace, had lost its last reader, and clang++ promotes -Wunused-const-variable to an error inside -Werror where g++ does not -- which is why the worker's g++ build was green and the gate was not. This is the same defect class that blocked five sibling packages in wave w1. Diagnosis: the fact the constant carried is NOT gone and was NOT deleted. The two places that genuinely need the receiver's extent had each grown their own second copy of the literal instead: the D7 guard-page placement (`mapping + page - 0x214`) and the D7 fill length. So the constant was orphaned by a duplication, not superseded by a lost fact. Fix, in sw1_0104c110_model_test.cpp only (the .cpp and the header were not touched; re_0104c110 still models exactly `MOV EAX,[ECX+0x210] ; RET` and still emits disp32 0x210): (1) two static_asserts pin the test's copy to the header's opaque run -- kReceiverBytes == sizeof(OpaqueVtableOwner), and kReceiverFieldDisplacement + sizeof(FieldWord) == kReceiverBytes; (2) the D7 guard-page boundary and the D7 fill length are now derived from kReceiverBytes instead of a duplicated 0x214, so the boundary that kills the over-wide-read mutants moves with the extent instead of agreeing with it by coincidence; (3) three runtime CHECKs were ADDED (64 -> 67 checks) stating that the receiver is large enough for every displacement the body reads, that the read ends exactly on the receiver's last byte, and that the arena is strictly larger than the receiver. No assertion was weakened, removed or relaxed: a set comparison of the CHECK expressions before and after shows zero removed and three added. Verification: the section-5 gate reproduction (clang++ -m32, ar+ranlib static archive, link, run) now exits 0 with '67 checks, 0 failure(s)'; g++ -m32 -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror still exits 0; the header still compiles clean as its own TU under both compilers. Mutation round re-run after the repair: 15 of 15 wrong implementations killed and the control survives, under BOTH g++ and clang++, with the three detectors this package is known for all still doing their job -- m5_overwide_read and m14_extra_field_read killed by 1 failure each (the D7 guard page), m2_twolevel killed, and m4_writeback_same_value killed by 2 failures (the D6b PROT_READ mapping, which is what sees a same-value write-back that a byte snapshot cannot). One disclosed pre-existing behaviour, unchanged by this repair and re-confirmed against the pre-repair source: m2_twolevel and m9_header_deref terminate the runner with SIGSEGV instead of printing a check line, because the D5 value sweep plants 0u and a two-level model dereferences that null in the parent process (the D3b shared-memory child channel covers the dedicated D3b block, not the D5 sweep). Both are still killed -- the recorded survival criterion is 'the model test exits 0' -- and the identical exit status 139 was observed before and after the repair, so this repair neither introduced nor masked it.
